To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the L protein of cardioviruses induces a cytosol-dependent hyperphosphorylation of nucleoporins that is associated with nuclear trafficking inhibition.
cardioviruses inhibit nuclear protein trafficking through the nuclear pore complex by a mechanism that involves L-mediated phosphorylation of nucleoporins.
L, a 67 to 76 amino acid (aa) viral protein with no known enzymic activity, inhibits nucleocytoplasmatic trafficking through phosphorylation-dependent modification of nucleoporins.
